advances: Assumes an actual nested mixed-volume enlargement with unchanged integer centroid base. The condition controls the continuous centroid motion.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: Write $c'$ for the new continuous centroid. The mixed measure of $D'$ dominates that of $D$; their difference $\nu$ has mass $\delta$. Subtracting first moments gives $c'-c=\int(x-c)\,d\nu/(m+\delta)$, so $\|c'-c\|\le R_0\delta/(m+\delta)$. It suffices to test caps through the new centroid. With a nonzero continuous normal normalize it to norm one and translate the cap parallel to pass through the original centroid. The changed threshold on every fiber moves by at most $\|c'-c\|$, independently of the base tilt. Fubini bounds lost old mass by $L_0\|c'-c\|$. With a pure-base normal both thresholds are equal. The old through-mark cap has mass at least $\beta m+\sigma$ and added mass is nonnegative. Thus each new cap has mass at least $\beta m+\sigma-L_0R_0\delta/(m+\delta)$, proving the sufficient condition. If arbitrarily small positive additions are possible inside the fixed bounded source, take a common finite $R_0$. For $\sigma>0$ a sufficiently small positive addition then gives a larger feasible extraction, contradicting maximality.
statement:
Use summed $d$-volume, $d\ge1$, on the integer fibers of ambient convex bodies inside a common source. Suppose $D'$ enlarges each positive fiber of $D$, adds mass $\delta\ge0$ to mass $m>0$, and has the same true integer centroid base $j$ as $D$. Write $(j,c)$ for the original centroid. Let $R_0$ bound $\|x-c\|$ on the added mixed mass and let $L_0$ bound the sum, over original positive fibers, of their respective maximal $(d-1)$-dimensional section volumes, using counting at $d=1$. For an old feasible threshold $\beta$ put
$
\sigma=\inf_{H\ni(j,c)}[\mu_D(H)-\beta m].
$
The enlarged body remains feasible whenever $\beta\delta+L_0R_0\delta/(m+\delta)\le\sigma$. In particular, a mass maximizer admitting integer-balanced enlargements of arbitrarily small positive mass addition must have $\sigma=0$.
title: An explicit cap slack budget for integer-balanced enlargement
